Retrieved 2026-07-19 via Exa. BBC published 2026-07-15 06:35 BST.

Cash-strapped Thames Water poses big test for Burnham.
- Thames Water a major early test of Burnham's ambition to bring key utilities back under "public control". He has previously called for it to be nationalised.
- Options: "special administration" (temporary govt control, officials run company, taxpayer may recoup cash if sold on) vs full nationalisation.
- Thames Water CEO Chris Weston told Reuters lenders "want to see what the new Burnham government thinks before providing more funding."
- Dr Heather Smith (Cranfield): special administration is "sort of a temporary public control... not the same as full nationalisation"; long-term nationalisation "would be a struggle" given infrastructure upgrade costs.
- Burnham (to The Guardian, via CNBC): "Public ownership is absolutely an option. I would say for Thames Water, that is what should be done."
- Burnham (Independent, 2 June, Makerfield): water "industry is broken... it is about a 10-year plan of more public control, more public ownership... Thames Water, I would say there's a very strong case for public ownership to sort out its problems."
- Thames Water: ~£20bn debt, serving ~16m customers in London/Thames Valley; in breach of licence for two years. Defra estimated £100bn to pay off shareholders and take on debt across the sector (disputed).
